correctness.rationale: Distinct ordered centers have interval Voronoi cells and ties of zero mass. An optimum cannot have an unused center: assigning it to a positive-length part of a used cell strictly improves squared error. For a fixed positive-mass cell the squared-error minimum is its centroid, so a strictly interior gap center must own positive mass from both components. The other two cells are confined to the outer portions of their respective supports; their positive masses ensure 0<u,v<L. Within-cell integration of a uniform segment of length t at density w/L gives w t^3/(12L). Pooling the two inner segments adds exactly AB/(A+B) times the squared difference of their means, with A=pu/L, B=qv/L and separation G+(u+v)/2. The splitting gains S_L=p u(L-u)/4, S_R=q v(L-v)/4 have min(S_L,S_R) at most L^2 min(A,B)/4. The pooling penalty is strictly larger even at G=L/sqrt(2), using AB/(A+B)>=min(A,B)/2 and u+v>0. Thus the proposed cost is strictly above L^2/12-max(S_L,S_R), which is at least L^2/12-L^2 max(p,q)/16. Midpoint allocation of two centers to the heavier component and one to the other achieves cost at most that last expression, since nearest-center assignment can only improve on within-component assignment. This verifies the universal proof, not just the rational sample. Independently integrated cell moments for the small-gap example: the three centroids agree and the distortion is 257/6000 versus the anchored 5/96, with no claim of global optimality. The theorem excludes only one point in each of the three regions and makes no optimal-separation or separate two-mean assertion.

value.rationale: The three-center obstruction resolves the exact conjunction in a named open question and covers a nontrivial range of shorter gaps where the outer centroid conditions alone would not rule the configuration out. The splitting-gain versus pooling-penalty comparison is a natural explanation of why an interior gap centroid cannot pay for itself in this range. Scientific value does not depend on treating the sufficient barrier as sharp or implying that all gap centers are excluded.
